newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Buyers shun Belgian shares ahead of long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Buyers shun Belgian shares ahead of long weekend.

text.p: Most leading Belgian shares slid on Wednesday, with dealers reporting a lack of buyers on the last day of the present two-week trading account and ahead of Thursday's market holiday.

Banks, financials and holdings -- the driving forces behind the bourse's recent climb to record levels -- were the main losers. By 0830 GMT Generale Bank lost 125 francs at 14,750. Kredietbank was off 75 francs at 14,000 and Societe Generale de Belgique shed 10 francs at 3,290.
The Bel-20 index was off 0.4 percent at 2,244.95.
Steels bucked the trend after Luxembourg's Arbed painted a bright outlook for 1997 and said it would pay a dividend on 1996 despite a 1.2 billion Luxembourg franc loss.
Arbed was up 75 francs at 3,575. Belgian rival Cockerill at 134 francs.
Analysts and traders still rated Arbed a 'hold.' Arbed was due to hold an analysts' meeting in Belgium later on Wednesday.
Fast food chain Quick also went against the flow, adding another five percent to gains made this week, helped by an upgrade by a Belgian brokerage.
